relations.myth: Kaveh confronts Zahhak and begins the revolt
relations.note: Kaveh recovers his son, tears Zahhak’s testimonial, denounces the court, and rallies a revolt.
Kaveh defeats Zahhak’s forces and joins Fereydun in defeating or killing the tyrant.
Some oral accounts make Kaveh capture, torture, kill, or continually guard Zahhak.

relations.myth: Kawa kills Dehak and signals liberation
relations.note: Modern Kurdish tradition makes Kawa kill Dehak with a hammer and light liberation fires.

relations.myth: Kaveh brings the uprising to Fereydun
relations.note: Kaveh leads the popular host to Fereydun and transfers leadership to the royal heir.
Fereydun enriches Kaveh’s leather apron with brocade, gold, jewels, and colored streamers.
After refusing kingship, Kaveh selects Fereydun and serves as his commander and administrator.
Storyteller and oral traditions credit Kaveh with forging the weapon used by Fereydun.

relations.myth: Fereydun sends Kaveh to Khavar and Rum
relations.note: Kaveh campaigns as Fereydun’s general to impose royal authority and collect tribute.
Qaren is named as Kaveh’s son and becomes a later hero and commander.
Qobad is named as Kaveh’s son in the later epic tradition.
Kaveh tries to kill his son for insulting royal authority, but relatives intervene.
The stable later genealogy makes Kashvad Kaveh’s grandson through Qaren.
A Kurdish verse Shahnameh summary instead names Kashvad directly as Kaveh’s son.
relations.source: Kurdish verse tradition collected by Enjavi

relations.note: Later epic genealogy traces Gudarz’s lineage back to Kaveh through Qaren and Kashvad.
Giv is presented as Kaveh’s descendant through the Gudarzian genealogical line.
The later genealogy makes Kaveh an ancestor of Bizhan through the Gudarzian line.

relations.myth: Jamshid reveals Fereydun in Kaveh’s dream
relations.note: In folk versions Jamshid appears in a dream and reveals Fereydun’s location to Kaveh.
Some storyteller recensions associate Tahmuras with the revelation of Fereydun to Kaveh.
